newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tatneft settles most tax debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tatneft settles most tax debt.

text.p: Independent oil company AO Tatneft has settled 365 billion roubles of its tax debts with the finance ministry using official tax exemptions, the finance ministry said.

"The Finance Ministry states that... Tatneft submitted documents necessary to process Treasury Tax Exemptions in the sum of 365.0 billion roubles," the ministry said in a letter to the company last Thursday, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
Tatneft was issued the exemptions because it provided oil and fuel to the agricultural sector on credit on behalf of the government, for which it has not yet been paid.
Last Tuesday the government threatened six big companies, including Tatneft, with bankruptcy in its latest effort to clamp down on massive tax evasion.
The government said at the time that Tatneft owed it 407 billion roubles in taxes, but Tatneft chief executive Rinat Galeyev said its tax debt was only 42 billion roubles.
Tax exemptions can be used to settle tax bills, but produce no real revenues for the government.
The International Monetary Fund says the system undermines fiscal policy and threatens Russia's ability to meet tax reveue targets under its $10 billion IMF loan programme.
